claims.claim: Eustathius of Antioch was a native of Side in Pamphylia who served as bishop of Beroea about 320 and became bishop (patriarch) of Antioch shortly before the Council of Nicaea in 325.
He was a leading opponent of Arianism and engaged in literary polemics against Arians from 325 to about 330, which led to his deposition and exile to Thrace, where he died, probably around 337.

The work “On the Saying, ‘The Lord Created Me’ (Oratio in illud Dominus creavit me)” is a homily on Proverbs 8:22 that survives only in fragmentary form in the Patrologia Graeca (volume 18) and has been edited in the CPG series (3354, 3369).
Eustathius wrote the discourse to refute the Arian claim that the Logos was a created being, arguing that the Word is uncreated and that only the human Jesus was born of a woman.
